title: api-gateway: routing + streaming-proxy buffer tuning, payload limits and OpenAI-compat tweaks for tool/function calls
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: We observed sporadic streaming stalls and OOM spikes in the API gateway during high-concurrency tool/function-calling workloads (notably when clients use OpenAI-compat streaming with large tool payloads). This PR adjusts routing buffer allocation, introduces per-route streaming chunk limits, adds a payload_size_limit enforcement path for function/tool calls, and updates the OpenAI compatibility shim to honor chunk boundaries and content-type headers. The goal is to reduce tail latency, avoid transient OOMs in the streaming proxy, and ensure structured output/tool-calls are delivered reliably across routing fallbacks. Work items: 1) routing: add dynamic backpressure hints and per-route buffer caps; 2) streaming-proxy: increase default max_stream_chunk_size to 64KB, add adaptive_flush_threshold based on active inflight requests; 3) payload limits: enforce 1MB default payload_size_limit for tool call bodies with opt-out via route config; 4) openai-compat: ensure streamed deltas for function calls are emitted as JSON-chunks with content-type application/json-seq and update fallback behavior to re-route to smaller-model variant when route buffer saturated; 5) tests: add integration tests simulating concurrent tool-calls with binary payloads and structured output checks; 6) rollout: feature flag gated and staged to 10% of traffic for two days before full rollout.

review_thread: Liam Chen: Can you add a guard to avoid increasing memory for low-memory hosts? Concerned about default 64KB across all deployments.
Maya Patel: Added adaptive_flush_threshold that scales down chunk size when host free_memory < 512MB; added test and config override. See streaming/proxy.rs commit.
Nora Alvarez: The json-seq output for function deltas looks good; please ensure we still support legacy newline-delimited JSON for older clients.
Maya Patel: Compat shim retains legacy ndjson path when client sends Accept: application/x-ndjson; added an e2e test covering both formats.
Samir Rao: How will routing fallback behave under sustained saturation? We should avoid thundering-herd re-routes.

Maya Patel: Router now attaches backpressure_hint to route selection; when saturated we prioritize models flagged as 'low-memory' and add jittered retry/backoff on re-route. Added metrics for decisions.
Nora Alvarez: CI flake on integration test noted; looks like a timing assumption in the test harness. Please make the flakiness assertion tolerant and re-run.
Maya Patel: Fixed flake by waiting for stream open events and lowered timing sensitivity. All tests pass locally before pushing.
Liam Chen: Approving, left minor doc wording nits. Performance impact looks positive on bench runs.
Nora Alvarez: Approving after tests stabilized.
ci_checks: integration-tests: initially failed (streaming_tool_calls.test timing) -> fixed -> passed
benchmarks: perf microbench shows 12-18% reduction in tail latency in our lab
release_notes: Optimize API gateway streaming and routing for tool/function calls: per-route buffer caps and backpressure, adaptive streaming proxy chunking (default 64KB with low-memory fallback), enforced default 1MB payload limit for tool calls (configurable per-route), and OpenAI-compat streaming improvements (json-seq chunks and chunk_size honor). Rollout gated by feature flag; no breaking changes expected.
notes_for_ops: Monitor metrics: routing.buffer_cap, streaming.adaptive_flush, streaming.chunk_drops, payload.limit_rejections. Default rollout 10% for 48 hours; feature flag: api_gateway.buffer_tuning_v1. If increased memory pressure observed, reduce feature flag percentage and/or set route.buffer_cap override to lower value.
docs_update: Updated docs/api-gateway/streaming.md with examples for route-level buffer_cap, payload_size_limit, and OpenAI-compat behavior. Migration notes included for customers using custom proxies.
security_considerations: Enforce payload_size_limit to mitigate large-tool-call abuse vectors. No auth changes in this PR.
